countsMean.frames: The sweep's own frame count, asserted by `check-evidence.mjs` against the frames on disk that fall outside any declared `supplementary` set - 825 at this commit - because the terms moved in this round's rebase and NOT in the one before it: 934 `.webp` are committed and the sixteen `supplementary` sets below account for 109 of them, leaving 825. Re-derived for THIS head and stated once. The branch's previous stamps described the tree it was REVIEWED on (648 swept frames off 757 committed, which was self-consistent at that head); the rebase onto `main` brought main's later merges - and their frames - without re-deriving the remainder, and the review instruction for this round was to re-stamp rather than pick a side, which is what this is. `main` moved once more while this round was running (`#118`, `#137`, `0.19.7`), so the remainder was re-derived against that tip too: it adds no committed frame and no story, and the figures are identical, which is worth stating rather than leaving to a reader to guess. Both terms are read from the tree rather than transcribed (`find docs/evidence -name '*.webp' | wc -l` and the summed `frames` of the sets below) and `check-evidence.mjs` fails when they disagree with it.
countsMean.surfaces: `capture-evidence.mjs`'s `STORIES.length` at the head above - 137 entries, of which 39 are this PR's run-panel surfaces. The branch's previous stamp said 122, which was that list's own length at the head it was reviewed on; the rebase onto `main` merged 13 further entries (the model-picker surfaces and the tool-row boundaries), and this round adds two more - `roster-members` for the roster's membership rule and `reader-child-controls` for the descend control's singular label. `main`'s later tip (`#118`, `#137`, `0.19.7`) adds none, so 137 stands at this head as well. `check-evidence.mjs` counts the list and fails a mismatch, so this field cannot lag its own source.
countsMean.themes: `THEMES.length` - the twelve brand palettes; the live pair is the two brand themes only, because it proves behaviour rather than colour.

Storybook can force the revealed class but not produce the hover, and a staged draft is store state a fixture would have to fake, so these are captured from the running app against an isolated seeded backend instead. supplementary.source: headless Chrome over CDP, driven by `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs`: the shipped `applyHistoryPage` reducer and the shipped `CanonicalTranscript` over a real durable history page read from one real session's `transcript.jsonl` in the local store (`--session` and `--anchor` are required arguments; the id is deliberately not committed)
supplementary.why: The story renders a TranscriptRecord this repository built, so it proves the component. This set starts one layer earlier, at the bytes `/v1/desktop/sessions/{id}/history` serves — the stored rows, serialised verbatim by `read_transcript_page` — and runs them through the shipped reducer, which is what proves the payload reaches pixels: the durable row's own encoding, the extraction of `provider_payload.details.diff`, the identity gate and the args-drop rule. It cannot be re-derived by the sweep, and the payload itself is deliberately NOT committed: the harness writes it to a temp file and deletes it. Re-run with `node scripts/diff-body-evidence.mjs --session=<id> --anchor=<row id>` (see docs/evidence/write-edit-diff/README.md).

The only frames in this tree rendered against a REAL /v1/desktop/usage response rather than story fixtures: 11 provider reports and 28 windows as the local backend actually returned them, which is what proves the ported view renders the wire shape and not merely its own fixtures. Storybook cannot produce them (the payload needs the desktop bearer), so the sweep cannot re-derive these two frames. Account identities are redacted shape-preservingly by the capture script; every number, window, tier, unit and staleness value is the backend's own. docs/evidence/chat-usage/README.md carries the re-capture procedure. RE-CAPTURED for review round 1 from the same real response (replayed via `--payload`, since this machine's backend now returns zero reports and cannot re-derive it): the committed pair was the evidence for the staleness-baseline and description defects, so leaving it would have shipped a picture of the bug beside its fix. ROUND 3: a genuine live refill was attempted (live=true&refresh=true with the server's own bearer, plus explicit per-provider asks) and the backend returned zero reports for every provider - its credential view currently has no usage-reportable providers - so these two frames remain one commit stale with respect to the round-2 fold treatment. The fold at this density is evidenced by the re-derivable `chat-usage--dense` story instead.

partialCapture.note: This set is not a full sweep and does not claim to be. Ten stories were re-taken in the two brand themes through the rig at :6055, one `--only=` run per story, with a backend permitted on the configured port (no captured surface talks to it): the two new frames and the eight whose rendering this round's fixes move. SIX of those ten came back with different bytes - twelve frames: `todos-implicit-phase` (the unnamed group's boundary), `reader-pending` and `reader-gone` (the two absence lines), `mcp-auth-required` and `mcp-unknown-status` (the tally's singular) and `mcp-disconnected` (the canonical projection's failure text on a problem row). The two new stories add four more (`roster-members`, `reader-child-controls`), so this pass wrote 22 frames in total and sixteen frames are new or changed on disk. `reader-live` was re-taken and came back byte-identical, which is stated in the README rather than claimed as a change: a still cannot carry a ticking number, and that is the one claim in this round whose evidence is a measurement rather than a picture. Every other frame in the set is untouched by this pass, and the rest of the sweep describes surfaces this change does not touch. `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` name the committed tree; `dirtyWorkingTree: true` is the record that the capture ran against the working tree (the frames and this manifest were uncommitted when it ran) rather than against the commit itself, and `head` is the commit whose source those frames are of. `head` names the commit whose source tree these frames ARE of — the last commit that changes the story set's own inputs, which is where the frames came from — while `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` must name the TIP's trees, because that is what `check-evidence.mjs` compares them against; the two differ by the rebase repair below and by this manifest's own commit, neither of which the story set renders. Three things are in that scaffolding: the interaction harness behind the keyboard walk, the re-ordered `mixedImplicitPhase` fixture, and — folded in by the same repairs that restored `main`'s echo and warm wiring beside this branch's streaming work — nothing the frames show. Only the fixture moves a pixel, and that frame was re-taken after it; the harness cannot change a picture, and the repair's two files are not mounted by any story in this set. The pass ran over a working tree, which is what `dirtyWorkingTree` records, and its `refreshedAtHead`/`head` values name the commit that tree's source corresponds to on the branch as it now stands, because the SHAs the rig recorded died with the rebase.
partialCapture.branchAddition: THIS PR added 27 run-panel surfaces and 54 frames as first drafted, six more surfaces and twelve frames in the review round, four more surfaces and eight frames in the design round, and two more surfaces and four frames in round 1's batched remediation (the roster's membership and the descend control) - 39 surfaces, 78 frames. The set is a NARROWED capture over a branch, not a sweep, so it does not move the swept total by itself; what moves the swept total is the tree: `main` now carries 934 committed `.webp` against the 757 this branch was reviewed on, and 825 of them are outside every declared supplementary set, which is the figure `countsMean.frames` states.
partialCapture.review: Round 1's batched remediation, against a QA round and a UX round that agreed on this head: the roster's membership rule (`§ 4`), the reader's ticking clock, focus into the reader as it opens, `Escape` bound where the trigger's focus can reach it, Back popping one level, the plan's unnamed group boundary, and the four copy minors (the MCP tally's singular, the descend control's name, the `pending`/`gone` absence lines, and the canonical diagnosis on a problem MCP row). The frames those fixes moved were re-taken in the runs above; the two keyboard states this round fixed are not frames at all and were measured over CDP in the real renderer instead (README).

reconciledNote: `frames` is the SWEEP's term and it is checked against the tree rather than asserted: `pnpm check-evidence` recomputes it from the `.webp` files on disk that fall outside every declared set, so this number cannot be right about a set that is wrong. A narrowed run writes `partialCapture` and leaves the totals alone except when it ADDS a surface; the two additions below are declared sets, not swept frames.
